newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee pulls back from peaks, still strong.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee pulls back from peaks, still strong.

text.p: Late profit-taking and origin sales at the highs knocked robusta coffee futures from their peaks which saw benchmark May rising at one stage by nearly 10 percent.
"London just keeps getting hit in the afternoon, goes up in the morning and comes down in the afternoon even though New York is stronger," one said.
But prices still managed to finish up on balance on earlier speculative buying although the second-position contract failed to make a constructive close above $1,600 a tonne.
May stood at $1,560 a tonne at the finish, still a $50 gain on the day, but well below its ceiling of $1,655.
It spent most of the session $100-$120 higher after opening $110 up against pre-opening expectations of $200 higher on paper.
Trading in London was volatile and profit-taking set in as New York retreated from an advance in late U.S. morning trade.
London's volatility was further compounded by the fact that many players were increasingly taking a short-term view on the market.
"A lot of people are trading it very short term, in and out for $10-$15 and I think that's what is beginning to make it volatile at the moment," said one.
Volume was an impressive 9,192 lots, dominated by May and July contracts.
The March/March differential between London and New York widened to 111 cents early in the day before holding at 107 cents by London's close.
There were no fresh market-moving developments.
In fundamental news, coffee berry disease and drought have hit Kenyan coffee production for 1996/97 and more damage is expected.
The pest problem was severe in June-July last year when the weather was wet and humid but the disease no longer posed a threat to Kenyan coffee bushes.
